title: feat(network): configure and measure public hub capacity
body:
Refs #1476.

## Summary

A larger peer target alone cannot sustain the public Hub tier. This change couples peer retention to finite physical connections, source accounting, receive credit, gossip mesh size and independent primary and worker serve budgets. It reserves capacity for DAO observers and committee peers while measuring public traffic and application progress against a frozen Linux qualification envelope. Validator validated-address protection and its required qualification remain in Launch scope.

## Changes

- **Coupled public-hub limits.** The selectable profile binds confirmed ordinary peers, protected identities, physical connections, receive credit, source accounting, gossip mesh size and primary/worker service admission. Provisional peers consume aggregate capacity; unresolved identities gain no protected retention privilege. Promotion and protected arrival enforce the limits immediately. The [operator guide](https://github.com/Telcoin-Association/telcoin-network/blob/ca02e454b4f2fa5f5e1a47db8e346fb1bec00666/docs/src/network/hub-capacity.md) documents selection, limits and reproduction.
- **Protected identities and connection lifecycle.** Distinct configured bootstrap identities reserve physical slots within the existing cap. Previous, current and next committee identities are installed before public admission. The staging integration adds committee seeding (#1526) and bounded node-record freshness (#1501) while retaining that protection before listeners start and through the worker epoch handoff. Signed-record retrieval and connection-specific publication preserve authenticated identity bindings, reject stale handlers and update advertised endpoints. A valid expired signed self-record may identify an already connected anonymous peer without restoring expired DHT ownership. Seeding retains each restored record's original fixed admission ceiling.
- **Bounded recovery under public work.** Public rejoin drains active client commands and quarantines uncertain state. Shared-NAT recovery uses the existing 29-second deadline; reconnect waits for logical removal and actual Swarm closure within eight seconds. Verified catchup targets retain authenticated epoch, number and hash through demotion, backpressure and shutdown. Distinct-signer, continuity and freshness checks remain enforced.
- **Node-owned admitted serves.** Admitted primary and worker sync streams and bounded shed responses survive epoch-handle shutdown. Consecutive handlers share stream, per-peer and shed admission pools, so outstanding responses keep consuming their original permits. Worker streams acquire those permits before entering a queue that survives the epoch receiver gap, with independent expiry and the original request-read deadline. RPC and gossip retain their epoch event lane, and ready lanes alternate. Transfer deadlines and node shutdown still terminate admitted work.
- **Bounded public gossip delivery.** Nodes with both a public peer limit and process budget forward validated gossip directly to connected, confirmed ordinary peers within their public allocation. Public peers retain ordinary admission and resource limits. Separate membership tracking removes them on disconnect, prune or ban and reconciles identity and trust changes, preserving protected-peer behavior. The configured mesh remains 12 / 8 / 16 / 4 for eligible peers, and cached-ID announcements and payload requests remain bounded.
- **Bounded phase evidence.** The collector writes compact JSON through a byte-counted writer. Phase evidence has a separate 24 MiB input limit; manifests and other metadata retain the 16 MiB limit. Duplicate-key, finite-number, canonical-digest and raw-artifact checks remain enforced. Regression tests cover large valid phase evidence, metadata rejection, partial-write cleanup and existing-file preservation.
- **Per-hub CPU intervals and strict raw binding.** Each whole-process CPU counter retains a monotonic read bracket before its HTTP scrape. Scoring divides each CPU delta by the current read start minus the previous read completion, requiring a positive interval no longer than five seconds. This conservative divisor preserves the 0.75-core threshold and per-interval headroom checks. Hash-bound raw telemetry must match the scored brackets, process identity, CPU ticks and recorded clock-tick rate. Malformed, blank, partial and duplicate-key CPU records reject; ordinary protocol-log parsing keeps its existing behavior.
- **Concurrent qualification and authenticated evidence.** The isolated Linux runner exercises all eight scenarios together, including 512 signed transactions, four distinct executed batches and primary/worker transfers. Evidence binds source, binaries, profiles, topology, resources, admission, native request identities, operation outcomes and raw protocol logs. Post-window producer fences require complete native start/terminal reconciliation.
- **Completion-aware final sampling.** During the existing 30-second drain, the collector wakes when the workload exits and requests fresh metrics for both hubs. The two-second scrape deadline and final producer-watermark gates remain enforced. Failed scrapes report the hub, elapsed time and remaining budget. A deterministic regression reproduces the previous fixed-cadence failure near the cutoff and verifies that an overrun still fails.
- **Complete, bounded gzip metrics scrapes.** The endpoint negotiates gzip from complete, bounded request headers and renders the full registry with fresh process hooks for each scrape. It sends a complete encoded body with the matching length, falling back to the full identity body if compression is unavailable. The collector accepts only identity or one complete gzip member, rejects trailing data and incomplete HTTP framing, and enforces the existing two-second deadline and 4 MiB wire and decoded limits. The nine new Python cases and eight Rust unit cases cover negotiation, framing, body preservation and deadline failures; the existing Rust endpoint test also checks a fresh gzip scrape. The body-deadline regression now uses immediate headers and a virtual clock that advances on each byte, avoiding socket-setup timing races.
- **Complete manual qualification and staging integration.** Two isolated shards of 38 and 37 cases are configured to exercise 75 Rust mutation controls and reconcile 225 logs. The original 70 controls retain their order; five new controls target worker ingress regressions. The required PR workflow preserves its main-only trigger policy. Staging candidates use an opt-in manual qualification route through `durable-e2e.yaml`, which calls a distinct workflow at the selected source commit and retains the complete code checks, mutation controls and live phases. Ordinary durable runs keep their existing behavior. The staging integration retains aggregate network metrics, per-service calibration and the newer retention, consensus, state-sync and storage changes alongside the public-hub profile.

Includes prerequisite PR heads #1448, #1493, #1495, #1496 and #1497. The staging merge `49877c35f6ab8ff61ea3d41c802f9487e62a3670` incorporates staging base `b6805f8a53d9b2f5fa0f48a789a3cbe513d7a5ad` into public-hub head `6bdf846ef83283251312da7a1a2f27c472db2b07`.

## Declared qualification envelope

The frozen Linux ARM64 run assigns each of two hubs one CPU and 3 GiB RAM, and the coordinator two CPUs and 8 GiB RAM. It includes four validators, two workers per hub, 64 ordinary public peers (16 behind one kernel NAT) and eight DAO observers. Links are 25 Mbit/s, 50 ms RTT and 0.1% loss. Baseline and candidate use the same identities, debug binaries and workload, with a frozen 600-second measurement window for each phase. Each hub must use at most 0.75 CPU cores and 2 GiB RSS, stay at or below queue depth 100, and continue successfully completing engine outputs within 15 seconds, including intentional empty outputs. The profile and thresholds have not changed.

Every scenario requires at least 99% success among eligible attempts, its minimum count and its p99 latency bound:

| Scenario | Minimum attempts | Maximum p99 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Public join | 64 | 8,000 ms |
| Shared-NAT reconnect | 64 | 20,000 ms |
| Gossip beyond direct hubs | 4,096 | 3,000 ms |
| Record lookup | 256 | 3,000 ms |
| Submit-URL lookup | 256 | 3,000 ms |
| Concurrent sync | 256 | 30,000 ms |
| Committee progress | 512 | 1,500 ms |
| DAO connectivity | 512 | 1,000 ms |

Committee cancellations are counted separately and may not exceed 35%. Every primary and worker allocation, reserved DAO connection, resource bound and application-progress gate must also pass. Failed operations remain failures, and the evidence reader rejects missing or inconsistent raw records.

## Testing

Current pushed source is `ca02e454b4f2fa5f5e1a47db8e346fb1bec00666` (tree `33c406e60bcd5b6eb8327155758939c26ebe495c`).

- Fresh [capacity qualification](https://github.com/Telcoin-Association/telcoin-network/actions/runs/37940162416) at this exact commit has passed code checks: 182 Python tests in 49.365 seconds, 2,725 Rust tests in 95.010 seconds with 44 skipped, workspace compilation and pinned `cargo +1.94 clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings`. Both mutation shards are in progress; live capacity qualification remains pending. The matching [QUIC handshake qualification](https://github.com/Telcoin-Association/telcoin-network/actions/runs/37940184188) passed. Independent artifact verification and durable passing evidence remain pending.
- On byte-identical Python source for this commit, `python3 -B -m unittest -v test_cpu_timestamps test_collect test_qualify test_committee test_committee_fence` passed 68 scoped tests in 4.383 seconds. Regressions expose the former false-high and false-low CPU verdicts, enforce the five-second CPU window, reject malformed raw telemetry even after recomputing its artifact hash, and preserve protocol-log behavior. A fresh paired baseline/candidate capture is required; old evidence lacks the mandatory process-read brackets and raw clock-tick binding.
- Previous CI118 [workspace, mutation and capacity validation](https://github.com/Telcoin-Association/telcoin-network/actions/runs/37914665470) passed prior-source code checks and the CI mutation gate: both shards and reconciliation succeeded for 75 controls. Independent verification of the aggregate mutation artifact remains pending. Live capacity qualification failed. A separate [read-only diagnostic](https://github.com/Telcoin-Association/telcoin-network/actions/runs/37933793608) authenticated the retained archive and read its CI-produced scoring report: the candidate passed all eight traffic scenarios, with one remaining failure, `hub-1: CPU headroom exhausted or process restarted`. Independent analysis of authenticated raw process counters and scrape timing bounds the sole reported CPU breach at no more than 0.581778343 cores, below the declared 0.75-core limit, confirming a false breach caused by the loop-start timestamp mismatch. The original CI118 failure is retained; independent full qualification remains pending. No capacity PASS is claimed. The required [QUIC handshake profile](https://github.com/Telcoin-Association/telcoin-network/actions/runs/37914679682) passed on the CI118 commit. Its archive is authenticated, with scenario verification pending.
- The CI118 code check passed 170 Python tests in 48.516 seconds and all 2,725 Rust nextest tests in 96.925 seconds with 44 skipped. The pinned `cargo +1.94 clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings` check passed. The preceding capacity run stopped before live qualification because the shutdown mutant did not compile. The compiler diagnostic showed that removing the production close call left `Closed` and `close` unused under denied warnings. The current mutation wraps `ExpiryOwner` construction in `ManuallyDrop`, retaining those references while suppressing destructor cleanup. Production Rust and the targeted Rust test are unchanged.
- Fourteen scoped Python harness tests passed in 0.378 seconds, including a guard that rejects the former mutant. Static review confirmed that the original 70 controls and the first 74 current controls retain their order; independent review found no active findings. CI reported the repaired `worker_ingress_unpolled_expiry_owner` mutant detected under denied warnings; its raw compile and targeted test logs still need independent verification. These Python harness checks do not replace Rust behavior validation.
- Five Rust regressions cover retained stream ownership across a receiver gap, shared pending/active limits, independent expiry, unpolled cancellation and fairness between ready lanes. The staging integration also fixes the pending Kademlia query handoff and adds a regression for retained record admission ceilings during committee seeding. CI118 Rust tests and Clippy passed in the workspace code check. Synthetic stream values do not replace live validation of the complete sender-to-handler path. Pinned formatting, whitespace and independent source review passed. No local Cargo build, Rust tests, Clippy or Docker run was performed.

The earlier [capacity run](https://github.com/Telcoin-Association/telcoin-network/actions/runs/37860402976/job/113626000920) remains an independently reproduced candidate FAIL. Its three failed worker requests coincided with the epoch receiver gap. Its canonical-height plateau contained successful empty engine executions. Fresh runs therefore declare successful engine completions as application progress before scoring; workload, profile, success thresholds and the 15-second limit remain unchanged. No historical run is retroactively qualified.

A genuine fresh candidate PASS and durable independently verified passing evidence remain outstanding. The maintainer must run the pinned second-machine attestation on the final commit before requesting review.

## Remaining completion evidence

- [x] Implement coupled operator limits, all eight concurrent scenarios, real transfers, deterministic transactions and the isolated Linux runner.
- [x] Implement bounded recovery and protocol observations, signed-record identity guards, confirmed ordinary admission and physical-close reconnect regressions.
- [ ] Pass current-source workspace/native tests, Clippy, QUIC scenarios and all 75 mutation controls.
- [ ] Obtain a genuine candidate PASS against the declared envelope and independently rescore the raw evidence.
- [ ] Publish durable, independently verified passing evidence and reproduction instructions.
- [ ] Complete the maintainer's pinned second-machine attestation on the final commit.
